items.title: Steve Angrum Interview, 1961-08-08
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...I never did hear any of him. [INTERVIEWEE] I never did hear too much of him either, but I used to see him around that time.

ctx.x: Yeah, he was rough. He was a terrible clarinet player, huh? When he was young, yeah. Oh, you could hear one time was Alphonse Piku. He played with Manuel Perez. He's dead now. In his dance band or street band? He used to play street band and dance band. No, no. Piku was rough. Well, Piku was the target of town. That's right. I mean, Piku was our best musician, you know, out of all them fans up there. He was a good musician. He was a musician. He was a musician. He was a musician. He was a better musician than all…
I've heard that he was. His father and uncle were too. He was an old Lorenzo and Papazio. I never did hear any of him.

I never did hear too much of him either, but I used to see him around that time. Yeah. Good kind of thing. Did you ever come across where Hader played the old Sam Lutre, Sam Lutre Sr.? Yeah, I don't know. I played with him. I played with him a couple times, you know. Yeah. Two clarinetes and a band? No, no. He played a ton of sax. Oh, yeah. And clarinet. Is that the old man or the young man that's living now? No, the young one. The young one was living now.
